title: Ballerina Trigger Construct Spec
description: Authoring rules for a Ballerina trigger service, spec version v1.0. Carries only what library introspection cannot recover: presence rules, cross-construct relationships, identifier semantics, and handler shapes for the non-concrete case. The canonical spec, its field reference (spec.md) and worked instances live in the ballerina-trigger-construct-spec repository.

version.description: Spec version this instance conforms to. Minor is additive, major is structural.

serviceTypes.description: Service type alternatives this connector exposes.

annotations.description: Annotation types referenced elsewhere, defined once.

rules.description: Constraints spanning more than one service type. Every subject must name its serviceType.

id.description: An identifier or a reference to one. Always starts with a dollar sign. A handler, param, or return id is hierarchical: dot separated segments scoping it under its owning construct, for example $service.onMessage.records.

deprecatedReason.description: Why this construct is deprecated, as prose. A generator emitting Ballerina puts it in the # # Deprecated doc section.

packageInfo.description: The package a cross module type comes from.

typeRef.description: A type reference. Either a plain name, or a constructed type given by shape plus the parts that shape is built from. Every type inside a composite is itself a typeRef and can carry its own packageInfo.

name.description: Unqualified. It belongs to the module this file describes unless packageInfo is set. Composite types use shape, so a name never embeds [], <> or a trailing ?. Only () and record {} are non identifier names.

builtin.description: Present and true only when name is one of Ballerina's own language types (the basic types, anydata, any, error, (), record {}, and similarly). Absent, never false, for a module type.

subtypeFamily.description: Present and true only where this reference stands for the named type and every introspectable subtype of it, not the exact type alone, such as http:StatusCodeResponse covering http:Ok, http:Created, and any user declared narrowing. Meaningful wherever a typeRef names a relationship a declared type must satisfy rather than the declared type itself: dataBinding's constraint, excludes, and envelope. Absent, never false, elsewhere.

oneOf.title: array
oneOf.description: An array terminates with nothing, so it has no completionType.

completionType.description: Optional. What the stream terminates with.

oneOf.title: readonly
oneOf.description: A readonly intersection terminates with nothing, so it has no completionType.

typeRefOrUnion.description: One type, or a union written as an array with the codegen default first.

then.description: With one service at most, two of the same type is already impossible.

id.description: Flat, since a listener nests nothing above it. $listener, or $listener1/$listener2 when a connector declares more than one.

doc.description: What this listener is and when a service attaches to it.

services.description: serviceTypes ids this listener can host.

multipleServicesAllowed.description: Can one instance of this listener host more than one service at all?

multipleServicesOfSameTypeAllowed.description: Can two of those services be of the same service type? Absent means unconstrained.

requiredImports.description: Side effect only imports, never referenced by name.

platformDependency.description: A jar the build must put on the classpath. No path here, that is the user's own copy.

version.description: May be a wildcard pattern such as 3.1.*

scope.description: provided keeps the jar compile time only, for example when a licence forbids bundling it.

nativeLibraries.description: OS specific libraries the JVM must load at run time.

acquisition.description: How to get an artifact no public repository serves.

nativeLibrary.description: Where to put it is determined by os, so it is not repeated here.

doc.description: What this service type is for. Required even when concrete, since the id/doc pair is what makes every construct in the file navigable on its own, not only what introspection cannot recover.

concrete.description: true when the type declares its own methods and they can be introspected.

identifierSpec.description: Present only when the identifier slot carries meaning.

backedByConcreteType.description: true means the type's own methods are the handlers, so nothing more is said here.

then.description: A concrete backed type omits options.
A resource function is identified by its accessor and path.
The user names each instance, so the name is always * and presence does not apply.

id.description: Hierarchical: the owning serviceType's id plus this handler's name, for example $service.onMessage.

name.description: The handler method name, or * for an open handler.

addMode.description: subset, the default when absent, is one fixed method name governed by presence. many is a shape the user instantiates repeatedly under names of their own choosing.

doc.description: What this handler is for and when it fires. Required: options only exist under a non concrete type, so there is no doc comment to introspect.

params.description: Order is meaningful. A param that must come first is listed first.

accessor.description: Resource kind only. The accessor in resource function <accessor> <path>().

path.description: Resource kind only. The path in resource function <accessor> <path>().

valueSpec.description: A constraint on one part of a resource handler's signature. No syntactic form is recorded, since the language already fixes what a resource path may look like.

values.description: Legal literal values. A single * means any value the language accepts.

id.description: Hierarchical: the owning handler's id plus this parameter's name, for example $service.onMessage.records. On an addMode many slot, names the slot itself, not each user named occurrence.

doc.description: What this parameter carries. Required for the same reason as a handler's doc. On a many slot it describes what one occurrence is.

addMode.description: many means the slot repeats, with the user naming each occurrence.

then.description: A fixed slot must carry its name, otherwise each generator invents one.

returnSpec.description: A handler's return type, grouped like a param since it can carry the same id/dataBinding/annotations facts. No name or presence, a return has neither.

id.description: Hierarchical: the owning handler's id plus the fixed segment returns, for example $service.onMessage.returns.

dataBinding.description: Present only when one union member is a user declared subtype the runtime serializes out, such as a resource returning anydata. Same shape as a param's dataBinding, direction reversed: outbound instead of inbound.

annotation.description: attachPoint decides which construct field holds the reference to this id.

rule.description: A named constraint from an open registry. An unknown rule id is skipped, not failed.
Registry id, for example structure.exactlyOne. Open vocabulary.

message.description: Diagnostic text for a consumer to surface.

prefer.description: Role a generator should default to. A hint, not part of the constraint.

subject.description: What a rule ranges over. kind decides the shape.

path.description: Field path inside the annotation record. More than one entry for a nested field.

oneOf.description: Addresses a handler option by its id, not its name: an addMode: many option's name is always *, indistinguishable from any other many option on the same service type, so only id addresses either case uniformly.
Addresses a param by its own id, not a handler-name/param-name pair, for the same reason as the handler subject.

dataBinding.description: Written inline on the param it belongs to. A set of independent typedesc variants that share nothing.

constraint.description: This variant's typedesc upper bound. One type, never a union.

excludes.description: Instantiations another variant already owns, so each declared type maps to one variant.

shape.description: How the bound type is embedded in the declared type.

form.description: bare is T alone, array is T[], stream is a stream of T, included splices T into a field of an envelope record.

element.description: For array and stream, whether each element is bare or included.

bindableFields.description: Fields of the envelope bound to this variant's typedesc. Every other field stays fixed.
